newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED PLAGUED BY EUROPEAN MIND GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED PLAGUED BY EUROPEAN MIND GAMES.

text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson is a master of psychological warfare but even he must be baffled by the mind games Europe has played with his side this season.

United's 3-2 home defeat by Derby on Saturday, just four days before they face Borussia Dortmund in the European Cup semifinals, was the latest example of what has become a gradually emerging pattern.
Whenever United have Europe on their minds, their league form goes to pieces. Whenever their attentions are fixed firmly on the defence of their English title, they are unstoppable.

Between December 4, when they clinched their place in the knockout stages of the European Cup, and March 5, when they crushed Porto 4-0 at Old Trafford in the quarter-finals, Ferguson's men rattled up 13 consecutive league matches without defeat.

But just three days after they swept past the highly-fancied Portuguese champions, the English champions stumbled to a 1-0 league defeat at struggling Sunderland in what Ferguson described as a hangover from their midweek victory.
The Scot must be hoping Saturday's loss to Derby does not signal the start of another "blip" -- as he likes to call them -- in his side's schizophrenic season.
United's first blip came in the autumn, and again Europe appeared to be to blame.
In late October, the mere prospect of two key Champions' League ties at Old Trafford sent United into tailspin.
They lost 5-0 at Newcastle and 6-3 at Southampton in the fortnight before their match against Fenerbahce, and then slumped 2-1 at home to Chelsea in the run-up to their game against Juventus.
It was only when they beat Rapid Vienna in December in their final Champions' League match that United's domestic form really took off and they motored to the top of the league.
The pressure on United to do well in Europe has, it seems, become almost unbearable.
It is 29 years since they won their solitary European Cup and everyone at the club feels another continental success is long overdue.
Ferguson, who joked after Saturday's match that United fans would be reaching for the valium between now and Wednesday, at least has a full squad to choose from for the match in Dortmund.
England internationals Gary Pallister, David Beckham and Gary Neville all returned from injury on Saturday and all are expected to play in Germany.
The Old Trafford pysiotherapists have done their job on the weary bodies of United's players. Now it is time for Ferguson to go to work on their heads.
